SOUTH KOREA’S POPULATION COLLAPSE IS UNPRECEDENTED

South Korea now has the lowest fertility rate in human history.

In 2025, the country’s total fertility rate dropped to 0.68 children per woman — the lowest ever recorded for any country.

Key facts:

•  Births continue to fall every year
•  Deaths now significantly outnumber births
•  The working-age population is shrinking rapidly
•  Schools are closing, military recruitment is becoming difficult, and entire towns are emptying out
This is no longer a slow decline — it’s a demographic freefall.
South Korea stands as the most extreme example of what happens when a highly developed, educated society stops having children. Even with aggressive government incentives (cash payments, housing support, parental leave), the trend has only worsened.
This is a warning for every developed nation. When birth rates stay this low for decades, the consequences become structural and extremely difficult to reverse.
The math is unforgiving.

“Starlink is how we are paying for humanity to get to Mars.”

Every new user, every subscription, and every expansion of the network directly helps fund Starship development — the vehicle that will eventually carry people and cargo to Mars.

Starlink isn’t just connecting the world today.
It’s helping build the multiplanetary future tomorrow.
The revenue from nearly 10,000 satellites and 9+ million users is fueling the biggest engineering project of our time.
This is one of the most elegant loops in tech history: global connectivity today, interplanetary civilization tomorrow.

STARLINK IS A LIFELINE WHEN EVERYTHING ELSE FAILS

When disasters strike and traditional networks go down, Starlink steps in — often within hours.

Elon Musk on Starlink’s role in crises:

“Whenever there’s some natural disaster, we provide people with free Starlink Internet connectivity. We don’t want to take advantage of a tragic situation. That would be wrong.”
This is why Starlink has become indispensable:
•  Restoring communication for first responders and hospitals after hurricanes, earthquakes, and floods
•  Keeping civilians connected when cell towers and power grids are destroyed
•  Providing internet in war zones, remote villages, oceans, and polar regions where no other service reaches
With nearly 10,000 satellites and growing, Starlink is proving that high-speed, reliable connectivity can be a basic human right — available literally anywhere on Earth.

WHY STARSHIP NEEDS TO BE SO MASSIVE: ELON MUSK EXPLAINS THE SCALE FOR MARS

Elon has repeatedly emphasized that Starship’s enormous size—nearly 400 ft tall, over 5,000 tons fueled, ~1,200 tons of propellant—is no accident. 

It’s engineered for the massive tonnage required to build a self-sustaining city on Mars, far beyond what smaller rockets could ever achieve affordably or practically.

“It’s designed to make life multiplanetary, otherwise extreme overkill for mere Earth sector activity! Starship fleet mass to orbit per year will be more than 1000 times all current Earth rockets combined, including Falcon. 
Necessary, for a city on Mars.”

This massive scale unlocks:
•  Hundreds of tons per flight to orbit (reusable 100–150+ tons, pushing higher in future versions) — critical for habitats, ISRU plants, power systems, and crew in fleet quantities.
•  Orbital refueling efficiency — Huge propellant volume means fewer tanker launches to fill up for Mars transit.
•  Rapid, high-cadence production — To deliver millions of tons over time, only a vehicle this big + fully reusable enables airline-like launch rates without bankrupting the effort.

Smaller rockets? They’d need thousands of launches for what Starship fleets do in dozens—impractical for colonization timelines. Size = necessity for the tonnage bottleneck.

Every test flight refines this beast. The path to millions of tons on Mars starts with building big. Which upgrade—V4 thrust jumps, stretched tanks, or fleet-scale cadence—has you most pumped? Let’s accelerate to multiplanetary. 🚀🔴🌌

Key improvements in Raptor 3:
•  No external heat shield (full regenerative cooling throughout)
•  Record thrust-to-weight ratio
•  Simplified design with fewer parts
•  Higher reliability and faster reusability
Elon Musk on Raptor 3:
“Raptor 3 engine is a very advanced engine, by far the best rocket engine ever made.”
This engine is the heart of Starship V3/V4 and brings us much closer to the rapid launch cadence needed for the Moon and Mars.
